name: Structure First
rules: pp3–8: HH/HL uptrend; LH/LL downtrend; identify RBD/DBD supply or DBR/RBR demand at the structural base and wait for its test.
pp9–13: monthly→daily, weekly→H4, daily→H1, H1→M15. At HTF zone test, require strong LTF clearing of prior structure, then retest the origin/new zone; SL outside that LTF origin.

pp14–19,24–27: target opposite HTF zone. Trendline break, 50 EMA and rejection/engulfing at zones are supporting confluences, never standalone entries. Additional entries/trailing zones are described, not loss recovery.
pp20–24: DXY/correlation applies to USD-related instruments when corresponding charts exist. Trade reaction after news rather than predict the release.
gaps: No numerical swing/base/strong-move definition, zone tolerance, sizing formula or maximum added positions.
A screenshot cannot prove institutional orders, future zone validity, news outcome or unseen DXY correlation.
visual_notes: pp4,6–7: schematics mark structure clearance and four base patterns; circles are subsequent zone tests.
pp11–12: daily supply contains the H1 structure break; entry is the NEW H1 zone retest, not an immediate daily touch.
p15: multiple continuation entries with stops moved above latest lower-high zone.
pp17–19,25–26: trendline/EMA/candle examples support an already established zone/structure narrative; numeric example levels must never be transplanted to a new chart.

name: CarlFx BluePrint
rules: pp19–25: clear HH/HL or LH/LL, BOS continuation or CHoCH reversal; no clear structure means no entry.
pp28–32: identify equal highs/lows or other visible liquidity, wait for sweep then BOS/CHoCH reaction; do not trade the first breakout.
pp34–43: quarterly accumulation/manipulation/distribution/reversal narrative is context, not a guaranteed time-based signal.
pp46–51: return to OB with rejection/engulfing/LTF break confirmation; SL outside OB; stated risk 1–2%, target at least 1:2.
pp53–66: three-candle FVG requires non-overlap of outer wicks, strong middle move, and a qualifying sweep/OB/MSS narrative. MSS is energetic structure clearance after manipulation.
pp69–79: wait for complete setup, do not chase, keep risk consistent, review losses.
gaps: OB construction, swing detection, strong-displacement threshold, exact target choice and session clock/timezone not fully specified.
p59 announces three FVG components but details only timing. p61 describes a previous lower low in an uptrend; p64/diagrams refer to HL/LH clearance. Keep this inconsistency visible.
Claims about banks and account growth are source assertions, not measured probabilities.
visual_notes: pp35–43: cycle diagrams across yearly/monthly/weekly/session examples illustrate narrative, not guaranteed future sequencing.
pp53–56: bullish outer-candle gap below/above strong centre candle and mirrored bearish example.
pp61–66: sweep ($$$), energetic MSS and subsequent FVG are shown together; a gap alone is insufficient.

name: Eagle Way by Bacardi FX
rules: PDF pp8–11: rectangle encloses at least 2–3 repeated touches/sensitive area. Respect/bounce suggests reversal; strong break/disrespect suggests continuation.
PDF pp37–45: after respect, wait for directional candle close above for buys or below for sells; do not enter from a rectangle touch alone.
PDF p45: analyse bigger timeframes down to H1; M30/M5/M1 are mentioned for scalping. Trendlines support the rectangles.
gaps: No precise close-reference definition, zone width, strong-break threshold, protective stop, target or risk sizing rules.
The PDF refers to 2–3 additional videos not in the repository. Their rules cannot be reconstructed from this file.
visual_notes: PDF pp16–17,22–24,28–30: rectangles span repeated reactions; black marks/arrows identify breaks, green arrows respected turns.
PDF pp32,35–36: continuation through zones and rising gold price; pp38,40,42,44: red zones/trendlines with sell-close examples. Existing position markers are examples, not permission to add orders.
Use PDF page numbers; printed internal page numbers differ. Some embedded screenshots are cropped, so exact unshown entry/exit prices remain unknown.

name: FSTRADERS
rules: pp5–6: London/New York sessions; Asian range as context. Source quotes London09:00 and NY13:00 RSA.
pp7–10: body-to-body Fibonacci on impulse, reversed for sells; entries at 0.618/0.705/0.79, profit scaling 0, targets −0.27/−0.62/−1. Liquidity above double highs must first be swept in sell example.
pp11–15: daily bias/power of three; bullish London, stalk 07:00–09:00 New York retracement, ideally ≥20 pips; if none by15:00 SA walk away; 62% retracement example.
pp16–18: institutional round-number areas00/20/50/80 are contextual confluence. Risk1–2% per setup and stop trading when target reached.
gaps: Table of contents promises OB, liquidity runs/voids, MS, signature/V75 and psychology mentorship chapters absent from this22-page introduction.
NY-to-RSA clock mapping is season-dependent; source gives fixed conversions. Do not silently invent a timezone schedule.
No complete SL placement or deterministic reversal/sizing specification. PO3 phase labels conflict between text/diagrams. Growth plan is hypothetical, not a backtest.
visual_notes: pp5–6: Asian range and session expansion examples. pp8–10: body-anchored fib retracements, liquidity sweep, OTE and negative extensions.
pp12–15: daily bar open/high/low/close diagrams and intraday liquidity run. pp17–18:00/20/50/80 horizontal levels; not evidence of future turning points.

name: Giant Killer Strategy
rules: pp3–8,21: M15/H1; mark prior-day high/low, extend zone into next day, wait for second M/W leg retest with rejection. H4/D1 structure is checked in summary; no retest invalidates setup.
pp12–16: M sells or W buys after second-leg rejection (pin/hammer) or neckline breakout. Rejection shadow at least twice real body, small opposite shadow.
pp17–20: separate false-break variant: break high/resistance then three bearish candles, sell after third close; mirrored break low plus three bullish closes for buy.
gaps: Document requires stops but does not specify their exact placement or a universal target; H1 example says hold day if no affecting news.
No quantitative equality/retest tolerance, day boundary, swing algorithm or news source. Claims levels always hold are not empirical evidence.
visual_notes: pp4–11: prior-day HOD/LOD retested next day on H1, M/W overlay and zones. pp12–15: neckline alternatives.
pp17–20: false-break beyond level followed by three opposite-colour closes; distinguish from ordinary two-touch variant.

name: Candle Range Theory
rules: pp1–3: at HTF support mark closed candle high/low. Next candle raids low and closes back above it; require subsequent close above raid candle high OR LTF MSS then retest buy. Mirror at HTF resistance for sells.
p3: bullish SL below raiding candle low or MSS low, TP CRT high/next liquidity; bearish SL above raid high/MSS high, TP CRT low/next liquidity.
p4: killzones/session raids improve context; CRT range may be previous-day/session range. Accumulation can require more than3candles.
gaps: No single mandatory timeframe pairing, zone algorithm, session schedule or retest tolerance; the two confirmation routes must remain alternatives.
visual_notes: p1: H4 candle range mapped to M15. p2: support raid on H2 with M5 MSS/retest and target opposite range. p3: bearish H4 raid and M5 entry/stop/target.

name: NJAT Structure & Timeframes
rules: pp1–4: LTF swings/ranges nest in HTF swings/ranges; observe closes across timeframes and build top-down/bottom-up narrative.
pp5–7: impulse is fast distance, correction slower; uptrend needs HL, not HH alone; downtrend needs LH, not LL alone. Range minimum3candles, premium/equilibrium/discount.

pp7–12: aggressive initiation breaks swing structure; reversal reaction/BOS then mitigation into new range creates HL/LH. Strong highs/lows show aggression, BOS and HTF mitigation; weak levels without significant BOS are potential liquidity.
gaps: Context/observation framework, not a fully specified standalone entry system. No numerical momentum thresholds, entry trigger, TP or sizing rules.
Claims BFI protection are narrative; screenshots cannot verify who placed orders.
visual_notes: pp2,4: HTF range contains LTF trends/swing reversals. pp8–10: HTF mitigation followed by LTF reversal and two ABC variations. pp11–12: strong versus weak highs/lows and aggressive versus corrective delivery.

name: NJAT Week 1 – Observation
rules: p1: watch live candle opens/closes across TFs, including H1/M15/H4; focus London/NY; observe actual delivery without forcing bias.
p2: annotate historical moves and supporting logic for practice, repeat observations; this is learning material.
gaps: No executable entry, SL, TP, invalidation, sizing or pattern definition. It cannot cast an independent directional entry vote.
Hindsight instruction selects trades that worked; it must not be presented as unbiased backtest evidence. Promised m1 continuation is absent.
visual_notes: Both pages are observation instructions; no additional chart-encoded entry rules.

name: One Pattern One Million
rules: pp4–12: identify HTF trend and strong impulse, then trade correction toward origin only after lower-TF reversal confirmation. Indicators:9EMA,21EMA,50SMA.
p13: pattern daily→H1/M15, weekly→H4/M30, monthly→daily/H1, H4→M30/M5.
pp14–16: clear previous LH/HL or blocking S/R, cross EMAs/SMA strongly, then retest/spike at50SMA before entry toward impulse origin.
p17: source describes high-risk barcoding/multiple simultaneous positions and30%risk or loss-budget sizing. These remain source descriptions, never automatically enabled by scanner.
gaps: No quantified impulse strength, MA source/shift/method settings beyond periods, precise SL or barcoding exposure cap.
p16 allows a small spike as structural clearance; original scanner policy demands body-close BOS. Preserve this conflict and WAIT if direction depends on wick-only break.
Profit/quadrupling statements have no underlying representative dataset in repo.
visual_notes: pp5–7: trend/impulse examples V100/V75. pp9–12: bullish/bearish impulse-return variants, targets towards origin, not last-digit predictions.
pp15–16: weekly impulse maps to H4, structure clearance then50SMAretest; screenshot alone does not supply hidden MA values or a protective stop.

name: Price Order Delivery by Fuad
rules: p1: observe unbiased multi-TF delivery between reaction/initiation zones; stacking is prolonged range, trend delivery is impulse-pause-impulse.
pp2–3: distinguish range accumulation from trending order flow; ask what happened and whether reaction had follow-through.
gaps: Observation material has no complete entry/exit, invalidation, required timeframe or sizing rules. It cannot independently authorize direction.
Linked TradingView examples are illustrations, not current prices or an execution data feed.
visual_notes: p2: boxed range followed by impulse and volume-profile context. p3: labelled trend and ranging delivery sketches; no numeric trade trigger shown.

name: Pabifx Domain 2
rules: pp8–13: establish weekly/daily/H4 bias, mark H4/H1/M15 turning zones. At least2trendline touches then third-touch entry example. Wait at key levels for rejection/reversal OR full break then retest; second retest discussed.

pp13–20: V/W/Z variants require prior high/low retest and rejection; no V/W/reversal pattern invalidates the V setup. S/R: buy support/sell resistance after rejection; hammer/shooting-star shadow at least2×body.
pp21–34: double/triple tops/bottoms, H&S/inverse require appropriate prior trend and neckline break; wedges/rectangles require completed directional break.

pp35–38: monetary pattern first break/retest, small pullback, second retest with rejection (H1/M15). PCP continuation can fail. Gap-fill discusses daily NASDAQ gap and technical vs fundamental cause, with differing outcomes.
gaps: Specifically NASDAQ/stock-index examples; cannot transfer US stock session/news assumptions to synthetic digit markets.
Fixed16:30SAopen is seasonal, no timezone calendar provided. Several SL/TP descriptions say prior high/low without precise side or buffer.
Gap-fill >90%claim has no dataset. Some chart labels (falling wedge/triple top 'Buy') conflict with accompanying text; report uncertainty rather than force entries.
visual_notes: pp14–18: previous high/low retest V/Z schematics and actual NAS100 charts. pp19–20: bullish hammer vs bearish shooting-star.
pp22–34: neckline and wedge/rectangle examples include mislabeled images; require current structure/candle proof.
pp35–37: second retest is marked as entry point after initial break/retest; p38 gap rules depend on an unseen cause if no news/context provided.

name: WCFX Supply & Demand Basics
rules: pp4–7: trend-aligned RBD/DBD supply, DBR/RBR demand; large-range departure candles, base is sideways/opposing candles; immediate and delayed tests are distinguished.
pp8–10,13: proximal at base bodies, distal at extreme wick; wait for test; sell-limit below supply with SL above distal, mirrored buy-limit above demand and SL below.
pp10–11,13: exit1:3risk/reward OR next opposing zone; stop loss if invalidated. Daily/H4/H1 shown; no universal mandatory pair.
gaps: PDF text layer is badly fragmented; full-page OCR supplement retained with original extracts.
Source calls NZDUSD H4 screenshot RBD though it is labelled differently in some diagrams. Limit entry wording depends on current bid/ask location and needs broker validation.
No numerical strong-candle/base threshold, retest tolerance, stop buffer or universal lot-sizing specification.
visual_notes: pp4–6: NZDUSD daily downtrend, supply origins and DBD/RBD blocks; p7 immediate vs weeks-later test.
pp8–9: proximal base body vs distal extreme wick; p10 H4 pending sell below grey supply, SL above and bearish projected target.

name: Lesson 2 – Trading Tactics
rules: Single long page: fresh EURCAD H4 supply, fast departure/large candles, doji base; distal upper shadow, proximal lower shadow. Assess RR and weekly context.
Weekly false break of resistance and next support frame example; require inside-bar signal at supply then sell after downside breakout; SL above supply, TP next support.
Source allows strong counter-trend zone with candle confirmation/RR; a later bullish pin does not prove an earlier setup won.
gaps: One historical example, no complete generic zone-strength algorithm, trigger buffer, sizing rule or data for claimed winning consistency.
RR1:7example is reward seven times risk, not doubling seven times as text claims. No guaranteed maximum losing streak.
visual_notes: p1 panels: strong departure, doji zone, risk/reward box, weekly false breakout then H4 inside-bar entry below zone/SL above/target support. News candle is hindsight, not entry evidence.

name: Lesson 3 – Trading Tactics
rules: Single long page: USDCHF H4 strong supply/departure breaking support, weekly downtrend supports selling; pin base distal upper/proximal lower shadow; assess RR(at least1:2or1:3guidance).
Wait for zone retest and doji/inside/pin/engulfing confirmation; close of first/second doji or later engulfing described. Stop10pips beyond zone for doji example, above zone for engulfing.
gaps: Text calls sell target next 'resistance' while chart arrow points below at prior support. Do not silently resolve this contradictory exit for automation.
1:8is an example, not fixed provider payout. No quantitative strength/freshness thresholds or generic sizing rules.
visual_notes: p1 panels: weekly downtrend, H4 broken support becomes supply, retest doji/doji/engulfing, stop above supply and drawn target at lower prior support.

name: Lesson 3 – Engulfing Bar
source: Lesson 3 - The engulfing bar as an entry signal.pdf
rules: Single long page: engulfing requires higher high AND lower low covering preceding candle RANGE, body engulfing is not mandatory.
At supply bearish engulfing close confirms sell; SL above zone/distal, TP next support. At demand bullish engulfing confirms buy; SL below wick/zone, TP next resistance.
Large bullish engulfing example allows50%range retracement entry for RR; freshness, strong departure/candle size and RRqualify zone.
gaps: Early paragraphs invert supply/demand and say bearish supply signal causes move up; later text and charts show bearish supply sell/bullish demand buy. Contradiction must be reported.
Final large-candle paragraph says close gives good RR yet prefers50%; no numeric 'large' definition or universal entry choice. Missing full parent course.
visual_notes: p1: four range-engulf examples explicitly allow body not covering body; USDJPYH1supply sell, demand buy, AUDJPYH4DBDsupply sell, USDCHFD1demand50%entry. Chart direction resolves neither ambiguity automatically.

name: Lesson 4 – Higher Timeframe Ranging
rules: Single long page: EURUSDH1downtrend approaches qualified demand; check daily double-bottom and strong range breakout for bullish HTF reversal.
Strong/fresh demand and RRassessment, then tailed-bar rejection on H1; buy after close, SL below demand, TP next resistance. Do not reject solely for local downtrend when confirmed HTF bias reverses.
gaps: Case study only; no numeric zone-strength/candle thresholds, lot sizing or fully defined daily range/reversal algorithm.
Original global scanner WAIT policy applies to current consolidation; this lesson concerns LTF pullback after HTF range BREAK, not permission to force direction inside unbroken range.
visual_notes: p1 panels: local H1range breakdown/pullback towards demand, daily double-bottom/range breakout upward, H1tailed-bar rejection at demand and next-resistance target.
